title: Remember Us, We Pray Thee, Lord
description: Remember Us, We Pray Thee, Lord in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 93, “Psalm 106:4,5”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Re-mem-ber us, we pray thee, Lord, With those who love thy gra-cious name, And to our souls that good af-ford, Thy pro-mise has pre-pared for them.

lines: Remember us, we pray thee, Lord,
With those who love thy gracious name,
And to our souls that good afford,
Thy promise has prepared for them.
To us thy great salvation show,
Give us a taste of love divine;
That we thy people's joy may know;
And in their holy triumph join.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
